 Shri Nand Kishore Tiwari - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Himanshu Tiwari - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/
 Order

This is the second application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.463/224 registered at Police Station Maihar, District Maihar, for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366,
376(2)(n), 376(3) of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 5/6, 4(2) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The applicant is in jail since 10.06.2024.
2.
The applicant's earlier bail application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 07.02.2025 passed in M.Cr.C. No.55838 of 2024.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that in the statement of victim's father (PW/3), it has been brought on record that the victim was a major and to substantiate his argument, learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that though the said witness went to get admitted his daughter in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:36945 2 MCRC-27217-2025 the school

,
but he was not having any knowledge about her accurate date of birth.
In paragraph-11 of his statement, he has also admitted that the difference of age between his son and daughter (victim) is of 5 to 6 years.

It is further submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that the prosecution has produced the victim's birth certificate (Ex.P/12) before the trial Court, but in the said certificate, it is not mentioned as to which authority has issued it; the same is torn in the mid and no specific date in respect of registration of birth of the victim has been mentioned.

Reading paragraph-15 of statement of the witness (PW/3), learned counsel for the applicant has also submitted that victim's father did not carry any document when he went to the hospital for obtaining the birth certificate of his daughter.

This witness, in his statement, has further stated that he obtained the birth certificate of his daughter prior to 16-17 years of recording the statement and also admitted that when the birth Ram Sushil Sahu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118808430/
1 certificate was prepared, the age of victim was 2-3 years and on that basis, learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that at the time of recording the statement of her father, the victim was aged about 19 years.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has further submitted that the victim's father (PW/3) has further admitted the fact that the birth certificate (Ex.P/12) is torn and does not bear seal of any authority and also admitted that he could not explain that the date of birth was mentioned by any official on his own or not.

sentences.text: At the last of paragraph-15 of his statement, he has also admitted that he could not state as to when the birth certificate was issued and which authority had issued it.

The said witness has not given any NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:36945 3 MCRC-27217-2025 document showing birth of victim in the hospital, discharge certificate or the outdoor slip of the concerned hospital to the police authorities.

In the statement, nowhere it is stated as to where the victim was born and on that basis, learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the victim was a major and consenting party, hence, the applicant be enlarged on bail as the victim has not supported the prosecution case.
5. Learned Panel Lawyer has opposed the bail application.

6. Heard the parties and perused the case diary.
7.
The birth certificate of the victim reveals that her date of birth is 27.11.2009.
As per prosecution case, the offence was committed with the victim on 21.05.2024 and thereafter, she got pregnancy.
Fetus and blood sample of the applicant were examined by the FSL and on that basis, has opined that the biological father of the fetus is the applicant and victim is biological mother.
Looking to the aforesaid factual aspect of the matter, this Court does not deem it proper to enlarge the applicant on bail.
Hence, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, this second bail application filed for grant of regular bail stands dismissed.
